statement.p: Find the Jacobian. \frac{\partial (x,y,z)}{\partial (s,t,u)}, where x = 4u-\left(3s+5t\right), y = 5s+5t+2u, z = -\left(5s+4t+4u\right).

static.solution: \left|\frac{\partial (x,y,z)}{\partial (s,t,u)}\right| = \left|\begin{array}{ccc} x_s \amp x_t \amp x_u\\ y_s \amp y_t \amp y_u\\ z_s \amp z_t \amp z_u \end{array}\right| =\left|\begin{array}{ccc} -3 \amp -5 \amp 4\\ 5 \amp 5 \amp 2\\ -5 \amp -4 \amp -4 \end{array}\right|. This 3 \times 3 determinant is computed the same way as for the cross product, with the entries -3,-5,4 in the first row playing the same role as \vec i,\vec j,\vec k. We get \frac{\partial (x,y,z)}{\partial (s,t,u)}= ((5)(-4)-(2)(-4))-3 + ((2)(-5)-(5)(-4))-5 + ((5)(-4)-(5)(-5))4 = 6.
